newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Talks on future of Maastricht airport due in April.
newsitem.headline: Talks on future of Maastricht airport due in April.

text.p: The future shareholder structure of the Netherlands' most southerly airport is to be the focus of talks between all related parties next month.

Cor Leverdingen, spokesman for Maastricht Aachen Airport's operating company, said that the talks will start after the publication of a new business plan outlining a future strategy for the airport, being complied by a joint working party between Maastricht and Amsterdam airport Schiphol.
The two airports have been collaborating on the report for the last few months, Leverdingen told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Their final report would embrace the findings of a Dutch government study published in the Netherlands earlier this year, which stated the Dutch state's intention to withdraw from ownership of all regional airports, including Maastricht. The report will also take into consideration the findings late last year of a Ministry of Transport ruling on Maastricht's expansion ambitions.

After a lengthy debate between the Dutch transport and environment ministries, Maastricht was permitted two passenger charter aircraft to land every night, its morning opening time for take-offs and landings was extended by half-an- hour to 5.00 AM every day, and it won planning permission for a new 2,500 metres east-west runway.

Maastricht is 34 percent owned by the Dutch government, 38 pct by the province of Limburg, and 18 percent by Industrial Bank Liof. The remaining 10 percent is shared between 21 provincial authorities, the Belgian city of Tongeren and the joint chambers of commerce of Maastricht and the German city of Aachen. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
